text:
micah: quick heads-up — found an edge case in the quota tests: when a customer is at their monthly token quota and we apply backpressure + grace policy at the edge, some requests are routed to Dedicated fallback and then get billed unexpectedly. i think the interaction between quota enforcement at the api-gateway and routing stage needs clearer boundaries.

sara: can you paste the flow that produced the billing? short repro is fine.

micah: sure — sequence was: 1) user hits hosted API -> 429 soft (grace window) 2) gateway applies backpressure, marks request for retry 3) router picks dedicated pool with fallback policy (policy: prefer available capacity) 4) request executes on dedicated and consumes tokens. logs: ```WARN gateway: soft_quota_exceeded user=acct_42 grace_remaining=15s
INFO router: fallback_chosen target=dedicated-pool-7 reason=backpressure
INFO ded-serving: start request id=req_9f2 cost_tokens=124```

jordan: ah, so the gateway's 'soft 429 + retry' policy is blindly retried by our routing layer. that should be illegal — we should never retry over a billing boundary without explicit credit check.

lee: agreed. long-term we need a contract between components: gateway -> routing -> serving. the contract should mark requests with an "allow-billing-escalation" bit. default false for hosted customers.

micah: thinking of two short-term fixes: A) gateway drops requests that hit soft quota (no retry), surface clear 429 body with next-available-reset and credit-topup URL. B) allow retries but only to cheaper fallback (smaller model) and never to Dedicated. which one is less risky?

sara: B is risky because it still charges. A seems safer and simpler. but we also have many customers relying on graceful degradation — they'd rather get a smaller model than a hard 429.

jordan: we could implement a hybrid: retry -> degrade model only if the request has the allow-degrade flag (opt-in per-route). otherwise return 429. that keeps billing boundaries intact but preserves opt-in graceful degradation.

lee: that maps well to product: make degrade opt-in via route config + feature flag. we should also add server-side enforcement: router must check auth token metadata for allow-degrade before selecting Dedicated or paid variant.

infra-bot: deploy queued: feature-toggle:quota-degrade-optin -> staging at 2026-06-05T10:12:00Z

micah: another subtlety: autoscaler signals capacity preemption. if a Dedicated node is reclaimed mid-request, we currently return 503 and client-side retries can push them back to hosted which may then hit quota. need to think about backpressure windows vs autoscale churn.

jordan: for autoscaler churn, we should prefer graceful draining + draining time budgeted into router selection. router should prefer nodes with drain_eta > 30s for latency-sensitive work. also prefer cached KV hits on stable nodes.

lee: architecture note: quota enforcement points (edge) must be authoritative for user units. routing decisions can be conservative read-only unless request metadata explicitly allows state transitions (billing change, quota decrement). make that an explicit header: X-Quota-Authority: gateway|router and only gateway may flip consumed=true.

sara: can we add a 'grace credit' bucket for customers to opt-into during outages? small token allotment that auto-refills monthly but is not allowed to trigger Dedicated fallback. product can sell it as 'soft-overage buffer'.

micah: yeah, and label it in billing as "grace-buffer" so finance can disambiguate. important for audit. also needs separate metrics: grace_used, grace_blocked, grace_escalated (should be zero).

jordan: on the implementation side, suggest leaky-bucket for per-customer rate limiting and token-bucket for monthly quota. the grace buffer is a separate token pool checked after bucket exhausted but before hard-block. config example: ```quota_config: { monthly_tokens: 1_000_000, burst_capacity: 2000, grace_buffer: 5000, allow_degrade: false }```

lee: tradeoffs: leaky-bucket is easier to reason about with autoscaling since it smooths spikes; token-bucket enables bursts. we probably want hybrid: token-bucket at gateway for UX (bursts) + downstream leaky enforcement to protect serving capacity.

micah: final ask: can eng-platform own a tiny RFC to codify the contract (headers, allow-degrade flag, grace semantics, metrics) so infra and router teams can implement safely? I'll draft a short RFC and include the flow diagrams and sample headers.

sara: please do. add our proposed default: allow-degrade=false for hosted, true for self-serve routes behind feature flag.

jordan: I'll add router-side checks to my queue. can we also add unit tests simulating cross-component retries? caught this because our integration test didn't simulate router-level retries.

lee: good call. add an integ test: simulate gateway 429+retry and assert router never escalates billing without header.

micah: thanks all — i'll open the RFC and post link when ready. :thumbsup:
